definition: A model in which only a subset of parameters or pathways are active for any given input, in contrast to a dense model where all parameters participate in every computation.
details: Sparse architectures, such as mixture-of-experts models, allow scaling total parameter count without proportionally increasing the compute required per input.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Sparse Model — is what makes everything else possible.
